key_insight: Intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites is governed by halide-p band positions relative to the valence band maximum, rather than atomic spin–orbit coupling strength.
engineering_relevance: Hole-gated CsPbI3 could provide controllable spin currents for perovskite spin–orbit torque devices, rather than directly improving solar-cell performance.
method: First-principles calculations on CsPbBr3, CsPbI3, CsSnBr3, and CsSnI3.
Analysis of spin Berry curvature from spin–orbit-split halide-p bands.
Evaluation of intrinsic spin Hall conductivity versus hole density.
evidence_signal: Calculations locate the contributing bands 1.1–2.6 eV below the valence band maximum and predict that CsPbI3 reaches p-GaAs-level spin Hall conductivity at hole densities accessible through electric double-layer gating.
watch_item: The predictions require experimental validation of gate-induced hole densities and spin-current generation in working devices.
paper_title: Origin and hole-density dependence of the intrinsic spin Hall conductivity in inorganic halide perovskites
